unit: standing humans (16960 z); plan distances divided by 1060

definitions.overlook: walkable neighbour 0.5-3.0 humans above a space of at least 5 square humans
definitions.ledge: sector under 0.6 square humans, touching a solid wall, 0.08-0.60 humans above a big neighbour
definitions.arch: MISNAMED in the first pass, kept here as a correction. Measured as 'a two-neighbour doorway sector with more than four corners' and reported as a shaped arch head. It is not: of E6M6's 112 such doorways, 82 have a ceiling EQUAL to both rooms they join, so there is no head to shape. The extra corners are in plan -- turns of 15 and 30 degrees, alongside the square ones -- so these are SPLAYED passages: a link that funnels or dog-legs rather than running as a straight square tube. Read the number as 'splayed connectors'.
definitions.pit: walkable neighbour 0.5-4.0 humans below a big space
definitions.silhouette: distinct ceiling heights, to the nearest 2048 z, among the sectors bounding one open-air sector

headline: The candidate is not short of verticality, it is short of verticality at body scale. Around its large spaces it has 26 raised neighbours: 23 are steps under half a body, 1 is a parapet, 2 are whole storeys away. E6M6 has 134, of which 78 sit in the 0.5-3.0 band and NONE is more than 8 humans up.

rise_bands_around_big_spaces.definition: walkable neighbours whose floor stands above a space of at least 5 square humans, bucketed by how far above
rise_bands_around_big_spaces.reading: Blood's verticality is something you can see a man standing on. The candidate's is either a kerb or a different floor of the building, and neither reads as composition from inside the room.

what_to_build: parapets and raised walks around the big spaces: the candidate has 1 where comparable maps have 20-80
ledges and plinths against walls: 0.7 per 100 sectors against E1M1's 7.5
shaped door heads: 10% of the candidate's doorways have more than four corners, against E6M6's 48% -- Build cannot curve a wall top, so a gothic opening is shaped in plan
stop reaching for whole storeys; put the difference in the 0.5-3.0 band

closest_maps_by_palette.why: nearly the candidate's exact footprint -- 1080 square humans against 1027 -- with 2.5x the sectors and 2.9x shorter wall runs. The single best control in the corpus.
the map named by hand; a good match but the E6 (Post Mortem) episode is closer on palette

episode_note: E6 here is Post Mortem. Cryptic Passage is not in this corpus at all -- it ships custom tiles, so a tile-histogram comparison against it would be meaningless anyway. Recorded because an earlier pass named the E6 maps Cryptic Passage from memory rather than from anything measured.

splay.reading: Blood's connective sectors turn. The candidate's are square tubes, which is the same fact as its 0th-percentile orientation variety and its wall runs being 2.9x longer than E6M6's.
